[1] 10 things to NEVER do after your break up.
[2] 1.
[3] Begging Them to Come Back

Nothing kills your self respect faster than begging for someone who already chose to leave.
[4] If they wanted to stay, they would have.
[5] Don’t give them the satisfaction of knowing you’re desperate.
[6] 2.
[7] Stalking Their Social Media

Checking their Instagram, Snapchat, or TikTok won’t give you closure.
[8] it’ll just make you feel worse.
[9] If they seem happy, it’ll hurt.
[10] If they seem sad, you’ll overthink it.
[11] Either way, it’s a lose-lose situation.
[12] 3.
[13] Trying to Be “Just Friends” Immediately

You’re not fooling anyone, you’re holding onto hope.
[14] Staying friends right away usually just drags out the pain and gives false hope.
[15] You need space to truly let go.
[16] 4.
[17] Jumping Into a Rebound

Sleeping with someone else or rushing into a new relationship won’t make the pain go away.
[18] You’re just distracting yourself.
[19] Eventually, those feelings will catch up to you.
[20] 5.
[21] Drowning Your Pain in Alcohol, Drugs, or Partying

Getting high or drunk every night won’t fix your heartbreak.
[22] It might numb you for a while, but it won’t heal you.
[23] You’ll just end up feeling worse in the long run.
[24] 6.
[25] Isolating Yourself Completely

It’s okay to take time alone, but shutting out the people who care about you will only make things harder.
[26] You need support, even if you don’t feel like talking.
[27] 7.
[28] Replaying Every Moment, Trying to Find What Went Wrong

Overanalyzing won’t change the outcome of absolutely anything.
[29] No amount of “what ifs” will bring them back.
[30] Let go of the need to understand everything.
[31] Sometimes, people just leave.
[32] 8.
[33] Pretending You’re Okay When You’re Not

Faking a smile and acting like you’re over it won’t actually help you move on.
[34] Let yourself feel the pain.
[35] it’s the only way to truly heal.
[36] 9.
[37] Rushing the Healing Process

There’s no deadline for moving on.
[38] Don’t compare your healing to theirs or anyone else’s.
[39] Take as long as you need.
[40] 10.
[41] Losing Yourself Over Someone Who Walked Away

They are not worth your self respect, your future, or your happiness.
[42] Focus on becoming the best version of yourself, not on someone who didn’t see your worth.
[43] In 5-10 years, you will look back and be so proud of how far you’ve come.

[1] They always come back..
[2] When you pour yourself into a relationship, into someone, when you shower them with love and respect and support, when you give give give and receive only 1% back and don’t even mind, when you don’t listen to what anyone says because you KNOW what you feel and you don’t want to lose it, when you ignore all the red flags excusing them and finding reasons behind them…..
[3] You lose the one you love.
[4] They’ll take you for granted, they’ll lazily adjust to the presence of the love you give, they’ll slowly but surely stop working for it.
[5] And then they’ll leave.
[6] Because at some point you’ll notice that they’re not involved anymore, they don’t give anymore, they just don’t SEE you anymore.
[7] And you’ll ask them why.
[8] And they won’t know why, they won’t even know why you’re asking all of a sudden, why are you so needy, so clingy, why?
[9] And you’ll blindly give more and more, naively hoping that some of it will come back.
[10] But it never does.
[11] And so they’ll leave.
[12] And you’ll find yourself broken, like the ground shattered underneath your feet and you’re just falling and falling, wondering what you did wrong, what you could have done different.
[13] You’ll hurt, and you’ll be in pain.
[14] But after some time, one day you’ll find, without realizing, that the bleeding wound they left you with has disappeared, leaving nothing more than a dull ache.
[15] And then, you’ll feel nothing at all.
[16] You will be numb.
[17] And you’ll start to breathe again.
[18] That’s the moment when they’ll come back.
[19] They’ll come back promising all you’ve ever hoped for, all they never gave, never did, all you ever wanted.
[20] Because in the time it took you to heal, they’ve realized they miss what you gave them.
[21] And so they’ll come back.
[22] And you’ll feel nothing at all.
[23] You’ll look them in the eye and realize they don’t affect you anymore.
[24] On the contrary, you’ll see them and ask yourself “how could you treat someone who loved you like that?
[25] How can you look at them, see only love and affection in their eyes, and treat them like shit?”.
[26] And you’ll despise them.
[27] You’ll finally see them for the person they are, and you won’t like it.
[28] And you’ll have only one answer to their will to start over.
[29] &x200B;

[1] How can I (29F) get over the fact that I'm not my best friend's (30F) best friend?.
[2] In 2013 after an exceptionally bad breakup and graduating from college, I moved to a New City and basically started my life over.
[3] After a few weeks of subletting, I found a roommate on Craigslist named Kasie (30F) who I hit it off with immediately.
[4] I've always been more of a 'boyfriend girl' in that I was with my ex from tenth grade until college graduation and he was basically my 'best friend' so Kasie was my first real girl BFF.
[5] We lived together for four years until Kasie moved in with her boyfriend Jason (32M) and we had the best time.
[6] We almost never fought and spent all of our time at home together.
[7] We are both incidentally from the same home state, have a lot of similar interests and personalities and complement each other in lots of ways.
[8] I get along super well with Jason too and they never made me feel like a third wheel.
[9] I have a larger friend group now in New City and (thankfully) lots of girl friends but Kasie is still my bff and we talk/text constantly, hang out weekly, etc.
[10] The problem: Annie (30F).
[11] Annie is Kasie's best friend.
[12] They've been best friends since their early 20s and are kind of a package deal.
[13] Annie is very cool and smart and funny and she and I are  good friends too and there's no competition between us or anything.
[14] She and I even hang out without Kasie sometimes.
[15] I can't stress enough that we all get along and that this isn't like the movie 'Bridesmaids' or anything!
[16] But...
[17] sometimes I feel really sad that Kasie is MY best friend, but Annie is hers.
[18] Kasie will refer to me as 'one of her best friends' but we all know that Annie is 1.
[19] If Kasie ever says something like, 'You're my favorite!' to Jason he laughs and says, "No, that's Annie.' If Kasie and Jason get married, Annie will be maid of honor, no question.
[20] Everyone kind of says 'Kasie-and-Annie' like they're one entity.
[21] They have very big and beautiful matching tattoos (though Kasie and I have matching tattoos too, but imagine it being something like a 1 inch potato because we're both from Idaho, whereas Kasie and Annie have gorgeous tattoos that cover most of their upper arm).
[22] I don't know how to get over this sadness.
[23] It feels really childish.
[24] Kasie doesn't ever make me feel left out and neither does Annie.
[25] I love them both.
[26] But I guess I'm just jealous that I'm not anyone's 'favorite' in the same way.
[27] It feels extra childish of me because I have a boyfriend and I know I'm his favorite, but I guess I just never got to experience having a girl BFF who also considered me her BFF like that.
[28] How can I be satisfied with being almost-the-best and not the best?
[29] ---
TL;DR: My best friend, Kasie, has her own best friend, Annie.
[30] How can I get over feeling like I'm second best?

[2] Focus on the fact that they objectively couldn’t give you the quality relationship you deserved..
[3] It doesn’t matter what the reason is.
[4] They ended it and the best way you can respect that is by making the conscious decision to make your life happy, independent of what happens in theirs.
[5] Every second you waste wondering if they still love you or miss you is a minute that you can spend pouring love into yourself and building a future that  you’re excited about.
[6] Hopefully, with time and effort, it can be with someone who actually gives you love, safety, and never makes you doubt yourself.
[7] By worrying about whether or not your ex misses you, you are still subconsciously telling yourself: “They need to choose me in order for me to feel validated.” Stop it.
[8] They do not define your value.
[9] Only you can make yourself complete.

[1] School basically ruined my life and I'm still not completely over it.
[2] I'm only making this so that I can tell someone about my trumma without being told: "This isn't the time." Or "I don't care." Or "that's not a very nice thing to say."

When I first started middle school I knew it wasn't going to fun, but holy shit I was not prepared for the absolute hell on earth that I was in for.
[3] Some relevant information is that I have autism and ADHD, now normally that wouldn't be an issue, I just think differently than everyone else.
[4] Because of this, I had an IEP.
[5] From day 1 of middle school I was fucking miserable.
[6] I have incredibly sensitive hearing, as in I can hear a phone charger from several feet away.
[7] So just imagine what a school bell is like for me, thankfully I've gotten used to the sound of the bell and the crowded halls, but back then, I was completely overwhelmed whenever I had to move between classes.
[8] It took a week for the school system to add to my IEP that I am not allowed to be in the halls while classes are changing, I was to wait until the halls cleared.
[9] This was great, I was able to avoid having a panic attack 6 times a day!
[10] At least that's what was supposed to happen.
[11] But the hall monitors/principal/half the staff of the entire fucking school, chose to be dicks about it.
[12] I was late to class!
[13] It doesn't matter that my document from the federal government said I was allowed to be late.
[14] The teachers never actually punished me for being late, but many did give me weird looks.
[15] But the real trouble came when I started getting bullied.
[16] Now I looked like the stereotypical geek, had no visible muscle, talked about video games a lot, and at the time, was noticeably shorter than many of my peers.
[17] A perfect target.
[18] This is about where the true colors of the school system are shown.
[19] You see I may have looked like an easy pick for bullies, but I also had pretty bad anger issues.
[20] So when someone tried to bully me, I simply fought back.
[21] Every.
[22] Single.
[23] Fucking.
[24] Time.
[25] The bullies got off scott free and I was punished.
[26] Even when the bullies actually hit me, I was the one in trouble.
[27] I know this because the school only had 1 time and place for detention and not once did I see any of my bullies there.
[28] Most of the time it didn't even get physical.
[29] They would insult me, I would tell them off, I'd get detention.
[30] It was infuriating.
[31] This bullshit made me have a shorter and shorter fuse, until eventually, I'd snap at anyone who even glaced at me wrong.
[32] The continuous harassment from my bullies, the massive double standard the school seemed to have, and the fact that I knew exactly what the problem was and continued to tell people about it, yet everyone always tried the same fucking thing over, and over, and over, yet still expected things to get better, eventually drove me over the edge.
[33] I fell into severe depression, closed myself off, had a near perpetual bitch face, and a large amount of suicidal thoughts.
[34] The only things I found that could at least distract me from my own misery and self loathing, were video games, and the book series Wings of Fire.
[35] Video games were the biggest help, for the small periods of time that I could play, I was actually happy.
[36] And no I'm not exaggerating when I say: the only times I was genuinely happy was when I was doing something involving video games, or Wings of Fire.
[37] Of course my parents only believed the school's side of things and would punish me when I had violent outburst, which at this point was a weekly thing, by grounding me from video games.
[38] This made my depression worse and my suicidal thoughts more common.
[39] I also never at any point tried to hide my suicidal thoughts, nor did I hide how I felt about the situation.
[40] I eventually learned that the only times people actually seemed to listen to me was when I was yelling and swearing.
[41] So I yelled and swore constantly, trying desperately to convey that I need help.
[42] Everything came to a head when the principal called my mom because, during a violent freakout, I had punched a member of staff, however it was the time of the attack that caught my mom's ear.
[43] You see, at this point my parents had begun to actually listen to me and actually trying to help me through this.
[44] And when my mom heard that I had an outburst in the halls, during the class change, in direct violation of my IEP, she was extremely pissed.
[45] Also, plot twist: my mom's a lawyer, specifically a child attorney.
[46] Needless to say, my mom was very interested in why I was in the halls during class change, I don't really know what happened between my mom and the school but I'd wager to say: it was glorious.
[47] Not long after, I was transferred to a different school.
[48] One that actually began to fix the problems that my old middle school caused.
[49] I met friends who had similar problems as I did(most of which I still regularly talk to years later), I got therapy, and the teachers in my new school actually listened to me when I had problems.
[50] While I have PTSD from my time at the first school that I don't believe I'll ever be able to get over, and it also gave me a major fear of being ignored, I am very glad to have not only amazing parents, but also now friends who have helped me through numerus PTSD attacks.

[1] 10 things to NEVER do after your break up.
[2] 1.
[3] Begging Them to Come Back

Nothing kills your self respect faster than begging for someone who already chose to leave.
[4] If they wanted to stay, they would have.
[5] Don’t give them the satisfaction of knowing you’re desperate.
[6] 2.
[7] Stalking Their Social Media

Checking their Instagram, Snapchat, or TikTok won’t give you closure.
[8] it’ll just make you feel worse.
[9] If they seem happy, it’ll hurt.
[10] If they seem sad, you’ll overthink it.
[11] Either way, it’s a lose-lose situation.
[12] 3.
[13] Trying to Be “Just Friends” Immediately

You’re not fooling anyone, you’re holding onto hope.
[14] Staying friends right away usually just drags out the pain and gives false hope.
[15] You need space to truly let go.
[16] 4.
[17] Jumping Into a Rebound

Sleeping with someone else or rushing into a new relationship won’t make the pain go away.
[18] You’re just distracting yourself.
[19] Eventually, those feelings will catch up to you.
[20] 5.
[21] Drowning Your Pain in Alcohol, Drugs, or Partying

Getting high or drunk every night won’t fix your heartbreak.
[22] It might numb you for a while, but it won’t heal you.
[23] You’ll just end up feeling worse in the long run.
[24] 6.
[25] Isolating Yourself Completely

[26] You need support, even if you don’t feel like talking.
[27] 7.
[28] Replaying Every Moment, Trying to Find What Went Wrong

Overanalyzing won’t change the outcome of absolutely anything.
[29] No amount of “what ifs” will bring them back.
[30] Let go of the need to understand everything.
[31] Sometimes, people just leave.
[32] 8.
[33] Pretending You’re Okay When You’re Not

[36] 9.
[37] Rushing the Healing Process

[39] Take as long as you need.
[40] 10.
[41] Losing Yourself Over Someone Who Walked Away

[1] people keep telling me I healed fast.
[2] this is what I did..
[3] My breakup happened in late March.
[4] We (I'm M30, she's F28) were together for 15 months.
[5] We moved in after 6 months.
[6] We were madly in love.
[7] Soul mate vibes.
[8] But it fell apart.
[9] Our separation was, by far, the worst pain I've ever experienced.
[10] I've broken bones before.
[11] I've had people close to me die.
[12] None of that came close to this.
[13] There seemed to be a neverending well of grief.
[14] Fast-forward to today, and I feel like a new person.
[15] It hasn't been that long, 106 days, but people keep commenting on how good I look, how different I am, and how "healed" I seem.
[16] Today, I'd like to share some things that helped expedite my healing.
[17] Of course, as we all say, healing is not linear.
[18] This will be different for everyone.
[19] Either way, I have come to this board for solace quite a bit during my breakup, and I'm hoping to pay it forward with this post.
[20] CRY - My 1 rule throughout the entire breakup: whenever I feel the need to cry, I WILL cry.
[21] I never held it in.
[22] Ever.
[23] Even if I was in public or with a friend.
[24] Oh, and when I was alone, I really let it flow.
[25] Ugly, ugly crying.
[26] I've never been a big cryer, but this breakup literally broke something inside of me.
[27] I have never cried so much in my entire life.
[28] It feels really good.
[29] EXERCISE - Ok, we've all heard this right?
[30] But here's the thing.
[31] Don't just exercise.
[32] Perform an exorcism.
[33] Every workout should feel like you're expunging demons from your body.
[34] Go hard at the gym.
[35] Go hard on your runs.
[36] Everything.
[37] I understand the benefit of being gentle and compassionate with yourself post-breakup, but the more you push yourself, the more you sweat, the better.
[38] COMMUNITY - Lean into communities you're already a part of or join new ones.
[39] This could be a local meditation center or a jiu-jitsu gym or a volunteer network.
[40] This could also be your preexisting friend group.
[41] Maybe it's your family.
[42] Maybe it's your book club for God's sake.
[43] Whatever it is, you need to find your people and be around them.
[44] The only case where this is not advisable is when your current communities are toxic (find new ones).
[45] DO SOMETHING NEW - Speaking of finding new communities, I made it a priority to liven up my life in new spaces with new people.
[46] I referenced a few in the aforementioned point.
[47] I got back into jiu-jitsu, I joined a new meditation community, and I got involved with Big Brothers Big Sisters.
[48] Hell, I even dabbled with a few new hobbies (film photography became the main one).
[49] My life became so utterly full that even if my ex wanted me back, I wouldn't have time for her.
[50] I'm too busy doing cool and fulfilling shit.
[51] SPIRITUALITY - This may not be for everyone, but I'll go into it anyway.
[52] I lost my spiritual identity when dating my ex.
[53] My spiritual journey began in 2016 (dipped my toes into Buddhism) but things got a bit more serious in 2020 (started to go a bit further).
[54] When I was with my ex, this entire part of my identity was kept hidden, as if I was ashamed about it (she was very secular).
[55] When we separated, I leaned into my spirituality more than ever and it has been a Godsend (lol).
[56] If you are uncomfortable with spirituality, or it just doesn't appeal to you, please remember that just about anything can be spiritual.
[57] All it takes is for you to give yourself up to something greater than yourself or to lose yourself in an activity where you're thrown into some sort of flow state.
[58] Hell, just meditate.
[59] That's a good place to start, right?
[60] No matter what you do, the key is to disconnect from the ego for just a little bit.
[61] SOBRIETY - This is just my personal opinion, but you should be avoiding alcohol, cannabis, and all other drugs/addictive substances.
[62] Be wary of addictive activities too.
[63] I essentially quit gaming after we broke up.
[64] Gave my Steam Deck and my Switch to my sister.
[65] Said she could hold on to them indefinitely.
[66] I also believe you should be abstinent for as long as you can.
[67] No porn, no hooking up.
[68] Feel the fucking pain.
[69] Don't obfuscate your suffering with another person's body.
[70] The essence of this point is to be wary of all distractions and attempts to numb yourself.
[71] THERAPY - I found a really great therapist a month before we separated and I've been with her ever since.
[72] I'm going roughly 2-3 times a month.
[73] Find yourself someone who does sliding scale rates (google it).
[74] This pricing method makes therapy much more affordable.
[75] Try to have it in person.
[76] JOURNAL - Or just write in general.
[77] Write as often as you can.
[78] I mix it up between my Notes app and a physical journal.
[79] The physical journal is for the more intentional stuff.
[80] The Notes app is when I just need to "word vomit" at precipitous speeds.
[81] Whatever you choose, this will help.
[82] COMPASSION - Forgive both yourself and your former partner.
[83] No matter what they did, and no matter what you did, every day should be an effort to create an environment of compassion for the both of you.
[84] No one is perfect.
[85] You did what you could with the tools you had.
[86] You each tried your best (sometimes our "best" looks like shit, but it's still our best).
[87] GRATITUDE - I sincerely believe our breakups happened for a reason.
[88] Looking back on mine, I'm starting to understand why.
[89] And so be grateful that you shared that time together and now be grateful that you have the opportunity to reinvent yourself.
[90] Seriously.
[91] There is so much wonder and beauty in the world.
[92] Embrace it all.
[93] Start finding value and joy in the small things.
[94] For example, film photography has taught me how fucking beautiful the world is.
[95] Sometimes I look at the facade of an office building downtown and think "Wow, that is some beautiful architecture" or "Wow, that is a beautiful parking garage." No joke.
[96] I'm out here feeling inspired by the dumbest shit.
[97] Honestly, I could keep going, but I want to end this post by giving you a reality check.
[98] DESPITE all of this shit, despite my "expedited" healing, even though I have done every single thing that all the books/articles/Reddit threads say...
[99] despite all this...
[100] I am still so sad.
[101] Yes, I am happy.
[102] I am happy because my life is full.
[103] I am happy because I have great friends, great opportunities, and great hobbies.
[104] But I am also sad.
[105] I am sad because I wanted to be with her for the rest of my life.
[106] I wanted to keep sharing inside jokes and laughter.
[107] I wanted to travel together, get married, get a house, and maybe even have kids.
[108] I'm sad because all the potential we had has been sucked into the void.
[109] And so the key, folks, is this:

You have to learn how to be both happy and sad at the same time.
[110] You can't outrun the pain.
[111] You can try and keep busy like I'm doing – sure, it's good to be busy with positive things – but you need to learn to embrace the pain and hold it alongside your happiness.
[112] Thanks for reading.
[113] If you needed someone to say this to you today, I love you.
[114] Take care.

[1] If you’re a dumper who regrets their decision but is too afraid of reaching out, read this..
[2] Time has passed, maybe 3, 6, 9 months… 1 year… and you realized breaking up was a mistake.
[3] You thought you didn’t love them anymore, you were overwhelmed, you were convinced it was the right decision and after some time realized it was not like that and regret what you did… You’ve worked on yourself and wish you could show them… So what now?
[4] I’ve seen so many comments and posts here of dumpers saying they regret breaking up but don’t want to reach out to their ex (despite them wishing they had them back) because they think their ex has moved on and they don’t want to bother them anymore because the ship has sailed… or because they’re scared… And it really pisses me off.
[5] Because you’re doing it AGAIN.
[6] You’re deciding for them, AGAIN.
[7] Look, I’m not going to judge you for whatever reason you had to break up in the first place.
[8] Everyone makes mistakes and we all do things we’re not proud of and you were probably going through things and thought at that time that it was the right thing to do, even if it wasn’t… That can happen, life isn’t easy and people make mistakes.
[9] But back then you made a decision, you decided to break up.
[10] And you (most likely) didn’t talk to your partner to explain how you’re feeling and talk about things and decide together what to do.
[11] No.
[12] YOU decided and informed them about your decision.
[13] And now you realized that it was a mistake and you wish you had them back but prefer not to reach out because of fear of rejection or because you think they’re happy now (which they might be!) or whatever.
[14] But reality is you’re making the decision again, alone.
[15] So please, talk to them.
[16] The least you could do is apologize for the things you did wrong.
[17] And then it’s up to them.
[18] Maybe they see how you’ve worked on yourself and want to try it out again.
[19] Or maybe not, maybe they’re happy without you and don’t want you back, in which case you’re not losing anything anyway but had the chance to apologize and take accountability for your mistakes.
[20] Either way, this time you didn’t decide for them and that’s a way to show that you respect them.

[81] Whatever you choose, this will help.
[82] COMPASSION - Forgive both yourself and your former partner.
[83] No matter what they did, and no matter what you did, every day should be an effort to create an environment of compassion for the both of you.
[84] No one is perfect.
[85] You did what you could with the tools you had.
[86] You each tried your best (sometimes our "best" looks like shit, but it's still our best).
[87] GRATITUDE - I sincerely believe our breakups happened for a reason.
[88] Looking back on mine, I'm starting to understand why.
[89] And so be grateful that you shared that time together and now be grateful that you have the opportunity to reinvent yourself.
[90] Seriously.
[91] There is so much wonder and beauty in the world.
[92] Embrace it all.
[93] Start finding value and joy in the small things.
[94] For example, film photography has taught me how fucking beautiful the world is.
[95] Sometimes I look at the facade of an office building downtown and think "Wow, that is some beautiful architecture" or "Wow, that is a beautiful parking garage." No joke.
[96] I'm out here feeling inspired by the dumbest shit.
[97] Honestly, I could keep going, but I want to end this post by giving you a reality check.
[98] DESPITE all of this shit, despite my "expedited" healing, even though I have done every single thing that all the books/articles/Reddit threads say...
[99] despite all this...
[100] I am still so sad.
[101] Yes, I am happy.
[102] I am happy because my life is full.

You have to learn how to be both happy and sad at the same time.
[110] You can't outrun the pain.
[111] You can try and keep busy like I'm doing – sure, it's good to be busy with positive things – but you need to learn to embrace the pain and hold it alongside your happiness.
